itineraries.title: 3 days in Dublin: history, lanes & legends
itineraries.subtitle: Walkable city routes from Viking foundations to coastal harbours
itineraries.summary: Explore Dublin on foot over three balanced days: Day 1 covers the medieval core and Trinity, Day 2 links the 1916 Rising with Georgian squares and the Liberties' brewing history, and Day 3 uncovers hidden libraries and Howth Harbour.

days.title: Medieval core, Trinity & the Liffey
days.description: Start early at Trinity College before winding through medieval lanes to Dublin Castle, Christ Church, and across the Liffey.

stops.title: Trinity College Dublin
stops.note: Enter through Front Arch early to enjoy Parliament Square before tour groups arrive.

stops.title: The Book of Kells
stops.note: Book a morning timed slot for the Old Library and the 9th-century manuscript.

stops.title: Dublin Castle
stops.note: Walk the Upper Yard and Dubh Linn Gardens where Dublin got its name.

stops.title: Christ Church Cathedral
stops.note: Step into the 12th-century crypt—home to the famous mummified cat and rat.

stops.title: Ha'penny Bridge
stops.note: Cross Dublin's 1816 cast-iron footbridge into the cobbled lanes of Temple Bar.

stops.title: Temple Bar
stops.note: Stroll Meeting House Square and hear how the quarter narrowly escaped becoming a bus station.

days.title: Revolution, Georgian squares & the Liberties
days.description: Trace Ireland's path to independence from O'Connell Street to Kilmainham, with Georgian architecture on the way and the Liberties' brewing history to finish.

stops.title: General Post Office (GPO)
stops.note: Look for the bullet scars on the Ionic columns from Easter Week 1916.

stops.title: O'Connell Bridge
stops.note: Pause on the only major European traffic bridge wider than it is long.

stops.title: St. Stephen's Green
stops.note: Walk the Victorian park where 1916 ceasefire pauses let the park keeper feed the ducks.

stops.title: Merrion Square
stops.note: Admire Dublin's finest Georgian doorways and the reclining Oscar Wilde memorial.

stops.title: National Gallery of Ireland
stops.note: Free entry—seek out Caravaggio's lost masterpiece, rediscovered in a Dublin dining room.

stops.title: Kilmainham Gaol
stops.note: Reserve tickets well ahead for the guided tour of Ireland's most storied prison.

stops.title: Guinness's 9,000-year lease
stops.note: Finish at St. James's Gate in the Liberties, where a 1759 lease ran for 9,000 years.

days.title: Hidden libraries, Phoenix Park & Howth
days.description: Trade the main thoroughfares for Ireland's oldest public library, Europe's largest walled city park, and a DART ride to the sea.

stops.title: St. Patrick's Cathedral
stops.note: Visit Jonathan Swift's cathedral and read his fierce self-written epitaph.

stops.title: Marsh's Library
stops.note: Tucked beside the cathedral—see the 18th-century reading cages where rare-book readers were locked in.

stops.title: Henrietta Street tenements
stops.note: Take the 14 Henrietta Street tour to feel three centuries of Georgian grandeur and tenement life.

stops.title: Phoenix Park
stops.note: Spot fallow deer in a park twice the size of Central Park.

stops.title: Howth Harbour & the 1914 gun-running
stops.note: Ride the DART 30 minutes northeast for sea air, harbour walks, and the 1914 Asgard story.

itineraries.title: Galway & Cliffs of Moher weekend
itineraries.subtitle: Colourful western lanes, karst wildflowers, and 214-metre Atlantic sea cliffs
itineraries.summary: A classic two-day West Coast escape pairing Galway's medieval stories and Claddagh heritage with the lunar limestone of the Burren and the dramatic Cliffs of Moher.

days.title: Galway city, Claddagh & Kinvara
days.description: Wander Galway's Latin Quarter before following Galway Bay south to a 16th-century castle on the tide.

stops.title: The Tribes of Galway
stops.note: Walk Shop Street and Quay Street to trace the 14 merchant families who shaped the city.

stops.title: Lynch's Window in Galway
stops.note: Find the stone memorial window on Market Street tied to Galway's starkest legend.

stops.title: The Claddagh ring
stops.note: Cross the Corrib to the Claddagh quay where the hands-heart-crown ring originated.

stops.title: Dunguaire Castle
stops.note: Drive 40 minutes south to Kinvara for golden-hour reflections on Galway Bay.

days.title: The Burren, Cliffs of Moher & Bunratty
days.description: Cross County Clare's limestone plateau to the Atlantic edge, returning via one of Ireland's best-preserved tower houses.

stops.title: The wildflowers of the Burren
stops.note: Pause along the R480 to see Arctic and Mediterranean wildflowers blooming side by side.

stops.title: Diarmuid & Gráinne's beds
stops.note: Visit Poulnabrone Portal Tomb, standing on the Burren pavement for over 5,000 years.

stops.title: Cliffs of Moher
stops.note: Walk south from O'Brien's Tower along the cliff path for quieter seabird views.

stops.title: Bunratty Castle
stops.note: Stop on the way back towards Shannon or Limerick to explore the 15th-century fortress.

itineraries.title: 5 days on the west coast
itineraries.subtitle: North-to-south coastal road trip from Donegal's cliffs to County Clare
itineraries.summary: Five unforgettable days down Ireland's Atlantic seaboard, linking Donegal's towering Slieve League, Sligo's Yeats country, Mayo's wild islands, Connemara, and the Aran Islands.

days.title: Donegal's fort, glen & sea cliffs
days.description: Begin in the rugged northwest, from an ancient hilltop ringfort to Europe's highest accessible sea cliffs.

stops.title: Grianán of Aileach
stops.note: Climb to the stone ringfort on Inishowen for sweeping views over Lough Swilly and Lough Foyle.

stops.title: Glenveagh Castle
stops.note: Walk the lakeside trail through Glenveagh National Park to the Victorian castle and gardens.

stops.title: Slieve League cliffs
stops.note: Take the shuttle or walk up to Bunglass Point for 600-metre drops into the Atlantic.

days.title: Sligo's Armada coast & Yeats country
days.description: Follow Benbulben's flat-topped silhouette past a 1588 shipwreck beach and Ireland's most famous poet's grave.

stops.title: The Spanish Armada at Streedagh
stops.note: Walk Streedagh Strand where three Spanish Armada ships broke apart in September 1588.

stops.title: W. B. Yeats at Drumcliffe
stops.note: Visit Drumcliffe Churchyard beneath Benbulben to read W. B. Yeats's stark epitaph.

stops.title: Sligo Rovers & the Showgrounds
stops.note: Pass through Sligo town and the Showgrounds, rooted in a 19th-century agricultural show.

days.title: Mayo: sacred peak, Achill & Cong
days.description: Journey through Clew Bay's island-studded waters and into the quiet woodlands on the Mayo–Galway border.

stops.title: Croagh Patrick
stops.note: Admire Ireland's holy mountain from Murrisk—or hike the lower shoulder for Clew Bay panoramas.

stops.title: Basking sharks of Achill Island
stops.note: Drive out to Keem Bay on Achill Island, once the centre of Ireland's shark-oil fishery.

stops.title: Grace O'Malley, the Pirate Queen
stops.note: Look out toward Clare Island, stronghold of the 16th-century pirate queen.

stops.title: The Quiet Man in Cong
stops.note: End the day in Cong village, where John Ford filmed The Quiet Man in 1951.

days.title: Connemara & the Aran Islands
days.description: Wind through mountain passes and bogland to the coast before crossing to Inis Mór.

stops.title: Kylemore Abbey
stops.note: Arrive early for mirror-still reflections of the neo-Gothic castle on Pollacapall Lough.

stops.title: Alcock & Brown's Atlantic landing
stops.note: Walk the Derrigimlagh Bog boardwalk to the exact landing spot of the 1919 transatlantic flight.

stops.title: Dún Aonghasa
stops.note: Take the Rossaveel ferry to Inis Mór and climb to the prehistoric fort perched on a 100-metre cliff.

days.title: The Burren, Cliffs of Moher & Inis Oírr
days.description: Wrap up the coastal drive across Clare's karst uplands and dramatic sandstone cliffs.

stops.title: The wildflowers of the Burren
stops.note: Explore the limestone pavements and hidden dry-stone valleys of Burren National Park.

stops.title: Cliffs of Moher
stops.note: Walk the coastal trail from Doolin or the visitor centre above the nesting seabirds.

stops.title: The Plassy wreck, Inis Oírr
stops.note: From Doolin Pier, spot Inis Oírr on the horizon—where the rusted MV Plassy still rests on the shore.

itineraries.title: Cork, Cobh & the Ring of Kerry
itineraries.subtitle: Maritime history, harbour forts, mountain lakes and a boat to Skellig Michael
itineraries.summary: Four days through Ireland's southwest: ring Cork's Shandon Bells, trace Titanic's last port of call in Cobh, explore Kinsale's star fort, walk Killarney's lakes, then take the boat from Portmagee to Skellig Michael.

days.title: Cork city, Blarney & Cobh harbour
days.description: Combine Cork's riverside character with Blarney's famous tower and the poignant harbour town of Cobh.

stops.title: The Bells of Shandon
stops.note: Climb St. Anne's tower in Cork to ring the 18th-century bells yourself.

stops.title: Blarney Castle & the Blarney Stone
stops.note: Explore the castle battlements, poison garden, and rock close.

stops.title: Cobh & the Titanic
stops.note: Walk Cobh's colourful waterfront—the final port of call for RMS Titanic in April 1912.

stops.title: Spike Island, Cork
stops.note: Take the short harbour ferry to the former fortress and island prison in Cork Harbour.

days.title: Kinsale's forts & the West Cork coast
days.description: Head southwest along colourful harbour towns steeped in naval and revolutionary history.

stops.title: The Battle of Kinsale (1601)
stops.note: Stroll Kinsale's narrow streets where the decisive 1601 battle reshaped Gaelic Ireland.

stops.title: Charles Fort, Kinsale
stops.note: Walk the Scilly coastal path out to the massive 17th-century star-shaped sea fort.

stops.title: The Lusitania & Kinsale
stops.note: Visit the Old Courthouse in Kinsale, where the 1915 Lusitania inquest was held.

stops.title: The 1796 Bantry Bay expedition
stops.note: Continue west to Bantry Bay, where winter gales thwarted Wolfe Tone's French armada.

days.title: Killarney National Park & the Ring of Kerry
days.description: Spend the morning by Killarney's lakes, then drive the Ring of Kerry west to Portmagee for the night, ready for an early boat.

stops.title: Ross Castle, Killarney
stops.note: Start by Lough Leane at the 15th-century O'Donoghue stronghold.

stops.title: Muckross House
stops.note: Tour the lakeside mansion and gardens framed by Mangerton Mountain.

stops.title: Killarney's native red deer
stops.note: Keep an eye on the meadows around Muckross for Ireland's only native red deer herd.

days.title: Skellig Michael by boat & Valentia Island
days.description: Landing tours leave Portmagee in the morning and take most of the day; afterwards, cross the bridge to Valentia Island.

stops.title: Skellig Michael
stops.note: Landing boats run from Portmagee mid-May to September and only in calm seas. Book months ahead and keep a spare day in case the trip is cancelled. The climb is 618 uneven steps.

stops.title: The puffins of Skellig Michael
stops.note: Puffins nest on the island from late March to early August, often right beside the steps. Give them space.

stops.title: The Valentia transatlantic cable
stops.note: Back on land, cross the bridge to Valentia Island, where the first transatlantic telegraph cable came ashore in 1858.

itineraries.title: Belfast & the Causeway Coast
itineraries.subtitle: Industrial pioneers, basalt columns, cliffside castles, and walled Derry
itineraries.summary: A compact two-day northern itinerary pairing Belfast's scientific heritage and Carrickfergus Castle with the Antrim Coast Road, Giant's Causeway, Dunluce Castle, and the intact walls of Derry.

days.title: Belfast's inventors & Carrickfergus
days.description: Discover how Belfast thinkers changed global physics and transport before heading up Belfast Lough to a Norman fortress.

stops.title: Lord Kelvin of Belfast
stops.note: See the statue of Belfast-born William Thomson (Lord Kelvin) at Botanic Gardens.

stops.title: John Boyd Dunlop in Belfast
stops.note: Trace John Boyd Dunlop's 1888 pneumatic tyre invention in Belfast's streets.

stops.title: Carrickfergus Castle
stops.note: Walk the sea-washed ramparts of one of Ireland's best-preserved 12th-century Norman castles.

stops.title: Andrew Jackson's Antrim roots
stops.note: Visit nearby Boneybefore, ancestral home of the seventh U.S. president's family.

days.title: The Causeway Coast & Derry's walls
days.description: Follow the dramatic North Antrim cliffs from rope bridge to basalt stones, finishing on Derry's 17th-century ramparts.

stops.title: Carrick-a-Rede Rope Bridge
stops.note: Cross the coastal rope bridge suspended 30 metres above salmon-fishing waters.

stops.title: Giant's Causeway
stops.note: Walk out onto the 40,000 interlocking hexagonal basalt columns formed 60 million years ago.

stops.title: Dunluce Castle
stops.note: Pause at the dramatic cliff-edge ruins where the lost 17th-century town lies beneath the grass.

stops.title: The walls of Derry
stops.note: End the trip with a full 1.5 km circuit atop Derry's unbroken 1618 city walls.

itineraries.title: 7-day classic Ireland loop
itineraries.subtitle: The complete first-timer's circuit: Dublin, Boyne Valley, Wicklow, Cork, Kerry, Clare & Galway
itineraries.summary: One week around the island, connecting 5,000-year-old passage tombs, monastic valleys, medieval castles, sea cliffs and lively cities, and back to Dublin across the Shannon.

days.title: Dublin essentials
days.description: Settle in with Dublin's essential landmarks on a compact city walking loop.

stops.title: Trinity College Dublin
stops.note: Begin in the cobbled quadrangles of Ireland's oldest university.

stops.title: The Book of Kells
stops.note: View the illuminated manuscript and the soaring Long Room.

stops.title: Ha'penny Bridge
stops.note: Cross the Liffey on Dublin's most beloved 1816 footbridge.

stops.title: Kilmainham Gaol
stops.note: Take an afternoon tour to ground yourself in modern Irish history.

days.title: Boyne Valley & ancient Meath
days.description: Drive 45 minutes north of Dublin into Ireland's ancient royal heartland.

stops.title: Newgrange
stops.note: Book Brú na Bóinne in advance to step inside a 3200 BC passage tomb older than the pyramids.

stops.title: The Hill of Slane
stops.note: Climb the hilltop overlooking the Boyne where legend places St. Patrick's Easter fire.

stops.title: Trim Castle
stops.note: Explore Ireland's largest Anglo-Norman castle, famously used as a set in Braveheart.

days.title: Wicklow Mountains & medieval Kilkenny
days.description: Head south through the Wicklow glens to Ireland's medieval marble city.

stops.title: Powerscourt Waterfall
stops.note: Stop at Ireland's highest waterfall tucked in a wooded valley at the foot of Djouce.

stops.title: Glendalough
stops.note: Walk from the 6th-century monastic round tower up to the Upper Lake.

stops.title: Kilkenny Castle
stops.note: Arrive in Kilkenny for an evening stroll along the River Nore and castle parklands.

days.title: Rock of Cashel & Cork harbour
days.description: Cross the Golden Vale to Tipperary's hilltop cathedral before reaching Cork.

stops.title: Rock of Cashel
stops.note: Arrive as the gates open to see the medieval skyline rising above Tipperary's plain.

stops.title: Cahir Castle
stops.note: Pause on the River Suir at one of Ireland's grandest surviving medieval fortresses.

stops.title: Blarney Castle & the Blarney Stone
stops.note: Walk the castle grounds and gardens just northwest of Cork City.

stops.title: Cobh & the Titanic
stops.note: Spend the evening by Cork Harbour where Titanic picked up its last passengers.

days.title: Killarney lakes & the Dingle Peninsula
days.description: Journey west into Kerry's mountains and out along the wild Slea Head coast.

stops.title: Ross Castle, Killarney
stops.note: Morning lakeside views across Lough Leane toward the MacGillycuddy's Reeks.

stops.title: Muckross House
stops.note: Explore the Victorian estate and Torc Waterfall trail.

stops.title: Gallarus Oratory
stops.note: Continue onto the Dingle Peninsula to see the dry-stone church that has stayed watertight for centuries.

stops.title: Great Blasket Island
stops.note: Visit the Blasket Centre at Dún Chaoin overlooking the uninhabited Atlantic islands.

days.title: Cliffs of Moher, the Burren & Galway
days.description: Take the Tarbert–Killimer car ferry across the Shannon into Clare and follow the coast north to Galway Bay.

stops.title: Cliffs of Moher
stops.note: Walk the dramatic cliff path above the Atlantic swells.

stops.title: The wildflowers of the Burren
stops.note: Drive the coastal road around Black Head through Clare's limestone terraces.

stops.title: Dunguaire Castle
stops.note: Stop at Kinvara for the tower house on the tide, rebuilt on the site of King Guaire's fort.

stops.title: The Tribes of Galway
stops.note: Spend the night in Galway City with live traditional music in the Latin Quarter.

days.title: Galway, Clonmacnoise & Athlone
days.description: A slow morning in Galway's old town, then east across the Shannon at Clonmacnoise and Athlone, and back to Dublin on the M6 (about 2 hours).

stops.title: Lynch's Window in Galway
stops.note: Find the stone memorial window on Market Street tied to Galway's starkest legend.

stops.title: The Claddagh ring
stops.note: Cross the Corrib to the Claddagh quay where the hands-heart-crown ring originated.

stops.title: Clonmacnoise
stops.note: Leave the motorway for the 6th-century monastic ruins on the banks of the Shannon, 20 minutes south of Athlone.

stops.title: The Siege of Athlone (1691)
stops.note: Walk to the Shannon bridge and the castle, where the 1691 siege turned on a few planks across a broken arch.
